title: Federal Reserve consumer credit — August 2026
scope: Seven prepared tables covering the quantitative tables on all three pages. Period frequency, seasonal adjustment, annualization, missingness and revision status remain explicit. Descriptive analysis of the supplied release, not a current-market update or personal financial advice.

tables.title: Consumer credit growth — seasonally adjusted annual rates
tables.note: Original release: August 2026, released October 7, 2026. Annual, quarterly and monthly periods are separate source observations; do not add them together. Q2/Jun/Jul 2026 revised; August preliminary. All original printed numbers and missing markers retained. Seasonally adjusted. Growth and flow series are annualized rates, not month-over-month percentages or monthly dollar changes.

insights.title: August credit growth slowed
insights.text: The reported seasonally adjusted annual growth rate was 1.9% in August, down from 4.1% in July: a 2.2 percentage-point decline. These are annualized growth rates, not actual monthly percentage changes.

insights.title: Revolving and nonrevolving credit diverged
insights.text: August revolving credit contracted at an annual rate of 4.2%, while nonrevolving credit expanded at 4.1%. July figures were +2.5% and +4.7%, respectively. The series should not be averaged without weights.

insights.title: Outstanding balances rose despite slower growth
insights.text: Seasonally adjusted total balances rose from $5,188.5 billion in July to $5,196.8 billion in August: +$8.3 billion, computed from rounded published levels. Revolving balances fell $4.8 billion while nonrevolving balances rose $13.1 billion. These rounded-level changes need not reproduce the published break-adjusted flow series.

insights.title: Annualized flows are not monthly borrowing
insights.text: The August seasonally adjusted total flow is $99.4 billion at an annual rate, versus $212.9 billion for July. The revolving contribution is −$57.4 billion and nonrevolving +$156.8 billion, both annualized. Do not describe $99.4 billion as borrowing during August.

insights.title: Credit-card APRs remain distinct from loan rates
insights.text: August commercial-bank APRs: 21.19% across all credit-card accounts and 22.36% for accounts assessed interest; 7.54% for 60-month new-car loans, 7.17% for 72-month loans, and 11.90% for 24-month personal loans. June/July entries are n.a.; no interpolation is used. These are aggregate reported rates, not a personalized lending offer.

insights.title: The release contains different adjustment bases
insights.text: August total outstanding is $5,196.8 billion seasonally adjusted on page 1, versus $5,162.9 billion not seasonally adjusted on page 2. Their difference is not an extraction error. Separate datasets preserve the adjustment basis.

insights.title: Interpret the publication notes
insights.text: The source marks August as preliminary and several earlier 2026 observations revised. Credit excludes loans secured by real estate; growth rates adjust for series breaks and use unrounded data. Finance-company July/August terms and memo loan categories are unavailable in places. All 3 pages of quantitative tables are represented, while footnotes are summarized here.

limitations: Prepared offline from the embedded PDF text, then checked against the rendered source. This is not a live Gemini run.
Values remain at the printed precision. Derived differences use those rounded published values.
No forecasts, credit recommendations, or causal claims are inferred.
